heading: Training & Coaching
intro: Practical, clinically grounded training for the people who hold others at work — managers, HR teams and colleagues who find themselves supporting someone in difficulty without ever having been shown how.
body:
Most workplace mental health training stops at awareness. People leave able to name the issues but no more confident about the conversation they are dreading on Monday morning. My starting point is the opposite: what do you actually say, and what do you do next?

Sessions are built around the situations your people are really facing. I draw on more than a decade of clinical practice and on contracted therapeutic work inside organisations, so the examples are recognisable rather than hypothetical — and the guidance is bounded by what is realistic for a manager rather than a therapist.

Knowing where your role ends matters as much as knowing how to begin. A large part of this work is helping people support colleagues well without carrying responsibility that was never theirs.

Every session is shaped to the organisation. Tell me who is in the room, what they are dealing with and how long I have, and I will put an outline together.

cards.title: Mental Health Awareness
cards.description: Foundational training for whole teams: what common difficulties actually look like at work, how to notice change early, and how to respond without overstepping.

cards.title: Training for Managers & HR
cards.description: Focused work with the people who hold formal responsibility — supportive conversations, reasonable adjustments, absence and return-to-work, and referral routes.

cards.title: Reflective Practice & Coaching
cards.description: Regular facilitated space for teams in emotionally demanding roles, or one-to-one coaching for leaders carrying the weight of other people's wellbeing.

items.text: Knowing where a manager's role ends

quote: "In 2024/25, over 900,000 workers experienced work-related stress, anxiety or depression — costing 22.1 million working days."

faqs.question: Who is this for?
faqs.answer: Any organisation whose people manage other people. I have delivered this work across sectors including media and manufacturing, with groups of varying sizes.

faqs.question: Is it delivered on-site or remotely?
faqs.answer: Either. On-site tends to work better for interactive sessions with smaller groups; remote delivery makes it far easier to reach people spread across multiple locations.

faqs.question: Can training be combined with therapeutic support?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it often is. Several organisations contract me for both — training for managers alongside confidential therapy available to employees. The two remain entirely separate: nothing from a therapy session reaches the organisation.

faqs.question: How is it priced?
faqs.answer: Per session or as a package, depending on scope. Get in touch with a rough idea of audience and format and I will send an outline and a quote.

cta.heading: Request a Training Outline
cta.text: Tell me who you would like me to work with, roughly how long you have, and what has prompted it. I will come back with a proposed outline and a quote — with no obligation.
